name: frontiers_absolute
note: the incident that motivated the package

name: relative_resolves_against_landing
note: relative content resolves against the FINAL landing URL, not the DOI

name: whitespace_is_trimmed
note: Agreed, but only because the Go side does the work explicitly. WHATWG URL strips leading/trailing ASCII whitespace itself; Go's net/url does NOT — base.Parse("   ") yields %20%20%20. landingmeta trims ASCII whitespace (space/tab/CR/LF/VT/FF, not Unicode spaces) before parsing so the two agree.

name: http_is_rejected
note: plaintext downgrade is refused on both sides

name: empty_content
note: Agreed, as of the extractMetaURL fix in extension/src/background.ts. Both sides reject empty content. It was NOT always so: this fixture originally pinned a real defect, where the extension evaluated new URL("", location.href), resolved it to the landing page itself, and handed that HTML to chrome.downloads.download as if it were the PDF — the adapter's article rule only checks that the meta EXISTS, so an empty one still classified. The extension now trims content, rejects it when empty, and additionally rejects a URL that resolves to the page itself; landingmeta rejects empty-after-trim before parsing. Note both runtimes still resolve "" to the base natively, so this agreement is two deliberate guards, not a language property — remove either one and the defect returns.

name: malformed_content
note: DAEMON-STRICTER, and a genuine language difference. Go's net/url rejects "ht!tp://%%%" outright ("first path segment in URL cannot contain colon"), so landingmeta treats the tag as advertising nothing and returns ("", nil). WHATWG URL in the browser does not throw: a scheme that fails special-scheme validation falls back to relative resolution, so new URL() yields https://publisher.example/ht!tp://%%% — a real, bogus, https URL the extension would then try to download. Verified in both runtimes.

name: duplicate_identical
note: same value twice is not a conflict

name: duplicate_conflicting
note: DAEMON-STRICTER: Go returns ErrConflictingPDFURL. The extension takes the first match, which is safe there because the page was already classified under the user's own session; the daemon is fetching unauthenticated HTML from the network and must not guess which of two targets is real.

name: name_must_match_exactly
note: HTML meta name matching is case-sensitive via querySelector; neither tag matches
